simple.meaning: שַׁיִן (shayin) is a Hebrew word meaning “urine.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: שַׁיִן (H7890) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Kings 18:27, with occurrences in 2 Kings, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שַׁיִן (H7890) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in שַׁיִן (H7890) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: שַׁיִן (shayin) / H7890 is traced through 2 Kings 18:27, Isaiah 36:12 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H7890. shayin or shen [ שֵׁין שַׁ֫יִן, ] noun [masculine] urine ; — plural suffix שֵׁינֵיהֶם 2Kin 18:27 = Isa 36:12 (both Kt; Qr רַגְלֵיהֶם מֵימֵי ).
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to urinate ;

occurrences.englishText: But Rabshakeh said to them, “Has my master sent me to your master and to you, to speak these words? Hasn’t he sent me to the men who sit on the wall, to eat their own dung, and to drink their own urine with you?”

But Rabshakeh said, “Has my master sent me only to your master and to you, to speak these words, and not to the men who sit on the wall, who will eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?”
